problem_type: Author target can change during human approval
symptom: Original runner submits despite changed storyboard after human confirmation; deleting a canvas node while validation is pending still reaches the executor; an already approved variants/batch stops silently when the user switches projects
direct_cause: Only project lifetime is checked after asynchronous confirmation; executor reads the graph before the awaited guard and resurrects missing nodes from initialNode; batch dispatch omitted the author guard when forwarding options to each node; interaction epoch guards are reused as durable author guards after submission, so correct UI invalidation becomes implicit batch cancellation
class_root: Interactive surface lifetime and durable approved execution identity are conflated; asynchronous submission must validate original author content, node existence and persistent project binding independently of foreground selection
affected_population: Original canvas single/variants/regenerate and original storyboard single/first-frame/batch confirmation
Original background text generation and recovery result delivery
internal_only_reason: Existing original runner and human confirmation boundaries
invariants: Captured author target is checked after confirmation and grant before submission
After author validation, each executor attempt must resolve the node from its original project graph; absent nodes or graphs must fail closed, never fall back to the initial snapshot
Every batch wave forwards the same captured author guard to each node attempt
After first submission, switching foreground projects never cancels remaining approved attempts; only actual author, target or grant invalidity rejects them
Background graph reads and outcome writes compare the captured immutableProjectUuid and projectGeneration to existing persisted identity fields
Immediately before executor admission, compare model-declared authored inputs from the freshly read original graph synchronously after asynchronous author validation

Generated dependencies within the approved plan are allowed only while the consumed result belongs to the admitted upstream run; manual history selection or another run output requires renewed confirmation
Background saves compare the expected binding inside the existing manifest transaction; a removed workspace never falls through to legacy project creation
Original run and plan owners must consume rejected progress/status delivery promises, propagate failures, and settle their queue entries even when the fixed workspace binding is rejected
A regeneration duplicate captures its approved inputs immediately after duplication, before grant minting awaits

Text content, generation mode and selection are approved inputs; a downstream node may consume generated text only when its current document digest belongs to the admitted upstream run; completed outputs also match its existing resultId

Within one admitted text run, retries accept only unchanged approved content or that same run's sealed streaming content; every attempt builds its text request and append base from the original run input, never a failed partial output. Manual body, mode or selection edits still reject before the next executor call.

door_reduction.why_not: Original canvas, storyboard actions, UI reads, background deliveries and repository readers have distinct callers; converge phase validation in original runner and persisted identity validation in original delivery owner instead of removing product entry points.

generality_proof: Original confirmations freeze inputs before approval/minting awaits and forward durable guards to the original runner. Background delivery validates persistent binding and atomic save. Text body digests have exactly one owner: the existing run record. Original stream/final content writes atomically update body and that run digest via nodeRunOutcomePatch; original editor rewrite application updates the matching resultId run digest and triggers the existing persistence boundary. Ordinary editing cannot reseal it. No second editable document, result digest, selection replay, or new execution/context owner is introduced.

prevention.failure_mode: Reject stale author target before paid submission
prevention.strategy: Separate pre-submit interaction and durable author guard types; keep per-attempt durable validation inside original runner; retain existing workspace identity in normalized records and validate it in original background read/write owner. Own streamed text is admitted only when its digest belongs to the same approved noncompleted run; mode and selection remain independent approved inputs. After validation against the actual surviving node, text retries use the run's original document as executor input so failed partial output cannot become a new prompt or append base.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Local filesystem and shared application schema invariant

migration: Retain existing workspace identity in normalized records. The existing GenerationNodeRunRecord owns one optional textDocumentDigest; GenerationNodeResult is unchanged. Original run projectId is declared in its schema to prevent schema-only stripping. Actual normalizeRecord already retains raw payload identity. Old runs without digest authorize only the unchanged approved text body; no new state owner or document copy.
residual_risks: Controlled filesystem/service and browser component tests do not establish packaged Electron or Windows acceptance; browser storage roundtrip is not a real Electron disk write

The unchanged baseline text streaming executor and IPC do not forward or consume the runner idempotency key and grant. Restoring the original network retry can invoke the supplier again; matching runner keys in controlled tests do not establish at-most-once supplier billing. This repair does not claim or implement a new payment contract.
